correction.text: unchanged shape, but held 1395-1429, not 1395-1401: the independent kingdom of Nanzan ended when Shō Hashi seized it in 1429

keyframe_review.note: Years only. Cliopatria ends Nanzan in 1401 and enlarges Chūzan over its ground from 1402 (the gazetteer shows Chūzan's 1402 cells contain the Nanzan cell). The page has Nanzan kings Oueishi (to about 1402), Ououso (1403?-1413), Tafuchi and Taromai (to 1429), and Ming investiture for Taromai in 1415: the kingdom lasted to 1429. The Chūzan dossier removes the Nanzan ground from its 1402 and 1422 shapes.

region.text: the south of Okinawa Island around Ōzato Castle and Itoman

ledger.note: 1314: the Lord of Ōzato declares Nanzan in the south of Okinawa. 'Nanzan first came into being in 1314 when Tamagusuku inherited the role of head chieftain of all of Okinawa'; the lord 'established himself in Ōzato gusuku near the town of Itoman'. The page gives the district, not an outline.

notes:
Written by Phase B agent jk-01-b on 2026-10-18 from three pages (budget 1-2: the Nanzan page, plus two cross-checks).

Cliopatria error: the Nanzan row ends in 1401 and Chūzan's 1402-1421 and 1422-1428 shapes include the Nanzan cell (gazetteer resolve: the intersection of Chüzan 1402 and Nanzan 1395 is one H3 cell, 253 km2), although every page opened keeps Nanzan independent until 1429. The keyframe verdicts extend Nanzan to 1429 and the Chūzan dossier removes the Nanzan ground from its shapes. The 1401/1402 date may come from the end of Shōsatto's line or Oueishi's reign (to about 1402); no page ties a change to it.

Disagreements within the Nanzan page: Shōsatto/Ofusato 1314-1398 (table) vs 1337-1396 (infobox); Taromai 1414?-1429 (table) vs 1415-1429 (infobox). The page's '1380' Ming date is not there ('shortly afterwards' after 1372; Ofusato at the Ming court in 1388). The Ryukyu Kingdom page gives Hokuzan's fall as 1416, the Chūzan and Nanzan pages imply 1419.

The page gives no month or campaign for 1429. Kumejima is not mentioned. The grid is coarse: the whole kingdom is one cell, so the shape only marks the district.
